note_text:
CHIEF COMPLAINT: Chronic right-sided low back/buttock pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: This is a 52-year-old female with a 14-month history of right-sided low back pain radiating no further than the buttock, without radiation into the leg. She localizes the pain consistently to a region just caudal to the L5 level, over the posterior right sacroiliac joint, and denies any lumbar midline pain. She reports the pain began after a fall onto her right hip 14 months ago, with no antecedent trauma to suggest fracture.

She has completed 8 months of structured non-operative management including NSAID and gabapentin trials with dose optimization by her PCP, activity modification (avoidance of prolonged standing and single-leg loading), and a formal course of active physical therapy (18 visits) focused on SIJ stabilization and core strengthening, all without meaningful sustained relief.

She denies widespread body pain, denies diffuse tender points, and has no history of fibromyalgia or somatoform pain disorder. No morning stiffness >1 hour, no psoriasis, uveitis, or inflammatory bowel disease to suggest a systemic inflammatory arthropathy.

PHYSICAL EXAM: Focal tenderness to palpation directly over the right posterior SIJ, reproducible and consistent. No tenderness over the greater trochanter, coccyx, or lumbar paraspinal region. No hip joint line tenderness.

Provocative testing: Thigh thrust test positive on right. Compression test also positive. Gaenslen's test positive on right. Patrick's (FABER) test positive on right. Distraction test negative. Overall 3 positive provocative maneuvers including thigh thrust.

Neuro exam of bilateral lower extremities: strength 5/5 throughout, sensation intact, reflexes symmetric, negative straight leg raise bilaterally.

IMAGING: 
- Plain radiographs of the pelvis/SI joints: no destructive lesions, no erosive or sclerotic changes to suggest inflammatory arthropathy; mild degenerative changes only.
- MRI SI joints: no evidence of infection, tumor, or inflammatory sacroiliitis.
- Plain radiographs of the right hip: no joint space narrowing, no osteophytes; hip osteoarthritis excluded as pain source.
- MRI lumbar spine: no significant central or foraminal stenosis, no disc herniation, no nerve root compression correlating with her symptoms; mild multilevel degenerative disc disease without neural impingement.

DIAGNOSTIC INJECTIONS: Patient underwent fluoroscopically-guided, contrast-confirmed intra-articular right SIJ injection with local anesthetic and steroid on two separate occasions (6 weeks apart). On both occasions she reported greater than 75% reduction in pain (VAS 8/10 to 1/10) for the expected duration of the local anesthetic (lidocaine), confirming the SI joint as the pain generator.

ASSESSMENT: Right-sided sacroiliac joint dysfunction, refractory to comprehensive conservative management, confirmed by exam, imaging exclusion of alternative pathology, and dual diagnostic injections with concordant response.

PLAN: Discussed percutaneous minimally invasive SI joint fusion given failure of appropriate conservative care and confirmatory diagnostic workup. Risks/benefits/alternatives reviewed. Patient elects to proceed with right SIJ fusion.
